content: Stupid question: why is the unit circle Circle while the (open) unit disc is UnitDisc and not just Disc? For uniformity, shouldn't both names either have Unit or not? There's also no standalone closed unit disc, which is sometimes useful. (Actually, here's a funny naming convention proposal: Disk means open unit disk, and Disc means closed (c!) unit disk?) Just a thought
Even better: we have unitInterval for Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, not Interval, and not UnitInterval... But I guess that's because it's a Set ℝ and not its own Type?

I prefer both to have Unit, i.e. rename Circle to UnitCircle.
Circle sounds like its the type of all circles, aka docs#EuclideanGeometry.Sphere

Regarding disc vs disk:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_disk
https://mathworld.wolfram.com/UnitDisk.html
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spelling_of_disc
https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/naming.html#spelling
For the second point, yes: unitInterval is "only" a term and not a type.
An advantage of disk over disc is that it can not be confused with the discriminant.
It's funny that the german word for discriminant is a direct transcription -- often, the correspondence is way less obvious.
German mathematics is its own different language, different from both German and mathematics...
